questions.q: This box is ___ than that one.
questions.why: Short adjectives add -er for the comparative, not 'more'.

questions.q: Today is the ___ day of the year.
questions.why: One-syllable adjectives take -est for the superlative.

questions.q: This film is ___ than the book.
questions.why: Long adjectives use 'more' for the comparative, never -er.

questions.q: She is the ___ student in the class.
questions.why: Long adjectives use 'the most' for the superlative.

questions.q: My grades are ___ than last year.
questions.why: 'Good' is irregular: good → better → best.

questions.q: That was the ___ meal I have ever had.
questions.why: 'Bad' is irregular: bad → worse → worst.

questions.q: He lives ___ from school than I do.
questions.why: 'Far' is irregular: far → farther/further → farthest.

questions.q: This bag is ___ than mine.
questions.why: With a short vowel + single consonant, double the consonant: big → bigger.

questions.q: She seems ___ today than yesterday.
questions.why: Adjectives ending in consonant + y change y to i: happy → happier.

questions.q: My new phone is ___ than the old one.
questions.why: Double the final consonant after a short stressed vowel: thin → thinner.

questions.q: Tom is as tall ___ his brother.
questions.why: Equality is shown with 'as ... as', not 'as ... than'.

questions.q: This test was not as hard ___ I expected.
questions.why: 'Not as ... as' compares two things showing they are unequal.

questions.q: ___ you practise, the better you get.
questions.why: The 'the + comparative, the + comparative' structure links two changes.

questions.q: The older he gets, ___ he becomes.
questions.why: Both halves of this structure need 'the' + comparative.

questions.q: I would rather have tea ___ coffee.
questions.why: Use 'than' for comparisons; 'then' refers to time.

questions.q: First we ate, and ___ we went home.
questions.why: 'Then' means 'next/after that'; don't confuse it with 'than'.

questions.q: Winter days are ___ than summer days.
questions.why: One-syllable adjectives take -er for the comparative.

questions.q: It is ___ restaurant in town.
questions.why: Superlatives of long adjectives use 'the most'.

questions.q: This road is ___ than that one.
questions.why: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -ow usually take -er.

questions.q: He runs ___ than anyone else on the team.
questions.why: 'Fast' is short, so the comparative is 'faster'.

questions.q: This is ___ chair in the house.
questions.why: Long adjectives form the superlative with 'the most'.

questions.q: Your idea is ___ as mine.
questions.why: To say two things are equal, use 'as + adjective + as'.

questions.q: She is ___ than her sister.
questions.why: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -ful take 'more'.

questions.q: This is the ___ book I own.
questions.why: Change y to i and add -est: heavy → heaviest.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'A cheetah is ___ (fast) than a lion.'
questions.why: Short adjectives add -er for the comparative.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'This is the ___ (good) day of my life.'
questions.why: 'Good' is irregular: the superlative is 'best'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'My room is ___ (big) than yours.'
questions.why: Double the consonant after a short vowel: big → bigger.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She is ___ (happy) now than before.'
questions.why: Consonant + y becomes -ier: happy → happier.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I am taller ___ my father.' (than or then)
questions.why: Comparisons use 'than', not the time word 'then'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'This chair is not as soft ___ that one.'
questions.why: 'Not as ... as' shows two things are unequal.

questions.q: This test was ___ than the last one.
questions.why: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y take -ier: easy → easier.

questions.q: It's the ___ interesting book I've ever read.
questions.why: Long adjectives form the superlative with 'the most'.

questions.q: The weather is getting ___ .
questions.why: Repeated comparative 'worse and worse' shows continuing change.

questions.q: She's far ___ experienced than her colleague.
questions.why: Comparative with long adjective: 'more experienced'; 'far' just intensifies it.

questions.q: The ___ you practice, the better you get.
questions.why: Parallel comparative: 'the more…, the better…'.
